unit.why: A first-person dream memorate (from the author's writings, apparently R. Yitzhak Isaac of Komarno) in which a soul questions him about his boasting phrases and he answers with humility.

stories.start_quote: עוד שם בח"ב (תנ"ו א) בעש״ק ישנתי
stories.end_quote: אמת אמת אמת חנני השי"ת עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: On a Friday afternoon nap the author dreams of a band of descending souls. One asks why he ends his Zohar interpretations with grand phrases like 'words given to Moses at Sinai'. He humbly explains that such phrases are the way of those who toil in Torah, who give thanks when they attain an insight. He learns that the boast is true but that he should refrain because of his enemies, and he thanks God for the holy souls who help him explain the Zohar truthfully.

tags.why: The whole account is a dream during a nap
